sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 5.4% a year from $114 billion in FY2016 to $184 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F177], but the path was a commodity cycle, not a trend.
Revenue fell 32.5% in FY2020 to $94.5 billion, then rose 64.7% in FY2021 and 51.5% in FY2022 to $236 billion [F5][F6][F7][D153][D192][D232].

The FY2022 jump came from higher upstream realizations and downstream margins [P57], and the FY2023 reversal of 16.5% to $197 billion [F8][D274] came from lower upstream realizations and downstream margins [P43][P44].
Revenue has now fallen three straight years, to $184 billion in FY2025, down 4.6% [F8][F9][F10][D358], on lower crude and refined product prices [P17].
The U.S. operating segment is the bulk of the top line, at 75.1% of revenue in FY2025 [D402], and it fell 5.3%, subtracting 3.9pp from growth [D403][D404].
Tengizchevroil was the offset, at 11.6% of revenue and up 16.5%, adding 1.5pp [D418][D419][D420].
Downstream was the drag: non-U.S. downstream fell 13.1% and U.S. downstream 8.5%, subtracting 4.9pp and 3.0pp from growth [D518][D519][D525][D526].
The volume side grew, with net oil-equivalent production up 12% on the Hess acquisition and TCO, Permian and Gulf of America growth [P28], but lower prices outweighed it [P17].
Profit fell faster than revenue: net income dropped 30.5% to $12.3 billion [F20][D359] while revenue fell 4.6% [D358], and diluted EPS fell 31.8% [D361].
Net margin was 6.7% in FY2025 [F30], below the 7.9% window median [D613] and far under the 15.1% FY2022 high [D612], though above the -5.9% FY2020 low [D611].
Cost of revenue fell 9.2% against a 4.6% revenue decline [D370][D358], cutting its share of revenue to 57.2% from 58.8% [D338][D296].
That cost decline came from lower purchased crude oil and product prices and volumes [P14], while SG&A rose 6.0% on the Hess acquisition and professional services [X50][D372][P13].
Below the line, the effective tax rate rose to 36.8% from 35.5% [D345][D303], and interest expense more than doubled to $1.2 billion [X80][X79], while net margin fell 2.5pp [D369].
Against peers, the 6.7% net margin sits at the 33rd percentile of six energy names versus a 10.2% median [F30][D631][D632].
Operating cash flow rose 7.8% to $33.9 billion [F60][D362], 2.76x net income [D346], as higher TCO distributions and Hess assets offset lower prices [P6].
Free cash flow was $16.6 billion, an 8.8% margin [F80][D343], just under the 8.9% window median [D616] and below the 13.4% peer median [D634].
Capex of $17.3 billion was 9.2% of revenue [F70][D342] and 0.86x D&A [D348], with 2026 organic capex guided to $18-19 billion [P4].
Working capital moved with receivables down 12.8% [D377] while inventory rose 7.0% [D378], and the filings cited do not explain the conversion.
Chevron ended FY2025 with net cash of $3.96 billion [D351], 2.1% of revenue [D352], after net debt of $156 million in FY2024 [D309].
That 2.1% ranks at the 83rd percentile of six energy peers against a -7.7% median [D352][D637][D638], with total debt down 60.5% to $3.3 billion [D350][D376].
Buybacks and dividends of $24.8 billion were 149.7% of free cash flow [D353][D354], funded partly by $11.4 billion of debt issued [X157].
The diluted share count rose 2.1% to 1,856 million [X122][D374], so EPS fell 31.8% against net income's 30.5% decline [D361][D359].
Revenue has declined three years running, from $197 billion in FY2023 to $184 billion in FY2025 [F8][F10][R1], driven by lower crude and product prices [P17].
Payouts have exceeded free cash flow for three years, at 132.8%, 179.7% and 149.7% [D270][D312][D354][R4], which is only sustainable while the balance sheet absorbs it.
The revenue basis is inconsistent: FY2025 is $184 billion in the table versus $189 billion as first reported [F10][X10][R3], so growth rates mixing recast and original years are not like-for-like.
Net income in the table is proxy-sourced and rounded for FY2021-FY2025, differing from the 10-K by up to 0.22% [F20][X20][R8], so precision-sensitive ratios should use the 10-K figure.
Watch whether revenue in FY2026 falls below the FY2025 level of $184 billion [F10]; a further decline would extend the three-year slide [R1], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Watch buybacks plus dividends against free cash flow: a ratio above the FY2025 149.7% [D354] would mean another year funded beyond cash generation [R4].
Watch net cash against the FY2025 $3.96 billion [D351]; a return to net debt would reverse the balance-sheet improvement that now ranks at the 83rd peer percentile [D637].
